newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open mixed, yield curve flattens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open mixed, yield curve flattens.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened mixed on Thursday, with the long bond reaching a new all-time high even as concerns that the Bank of Canada will hike rates weighed on the short end of the yield curve, analysts said.

"The trend is for curve flattening. The economic numbers coming out of Canada show definite signs of accelerating economic activity, and what goes along with that will be rate hikes by the Bank of Canada," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Service Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.08 to C$120.07 to yield a record-low of 6.472 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.48 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to negative one basis point from a positive spread of one basis point at Wednesday's close.
Analysts said the move higher in the long bond is the continuation of a longer-term trend, which got a boost from tame U.S. inflation data out yesterday.

The Canadian consumer price index report for June out this morning had no major impact on bond prices, dealers said. The report showed the so-called core CPI rose 0.2 percent on the month and 2.0 percent on the year.
At the short end of the yield curve, concern that the Bank of Canada will soon hike interest rates is weighing on both T-bill and shorter-term bond prices.

Rate hike speculation has been reawakened by a stream of strong Canadian economic data in recent weeks. The Bank of Canada last hiked interest rates on June 26, its first such move in more than two years.
"I'm expecting the Bank of Canada to hike interest rates another 50 to 75 basis points by the end of this year," said Allan.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond jumped C$0.07 to C$110.00 to yield 5.897 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.19 percent.
The negative spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 29 basis points from a spread of 28 basis points on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.27 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.20 percent.
